title: Eveready Industries India Ltd - 531508 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Eveready FY26 revenue grew 8.2% and EBITDA margin held at 11.5%; Jammu alkaline plant (INR200 crore, 360 mn units peak) inaugurated 22 April 2026.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue grew 8.2% and EBITDA grew 8.9%, with full-year EBITDA margin at 11.5% despite steep zinc cost increases in H2. Batteries grew 9.3%, flashlights 3% and lighting about 8.1%, with calibrated price hikes in carbon zinc and alkaline. The Jammu alkaline battery plant was inaugurated on 22 April 2026 and commercial production is expected within weeks. Management guided to holding margins near 11.5% in FY27, and debt was reduced by over INR100 crore in FY26 with further reduction targeted, helped by Noida leasehold sales.

financial_highlights.value: about INR116 crore (leasehold transfer completed 30 March 2026)
about INR136 crore (INR44 crore advance received)

segments.name: Batteries
segments.commentary: Grew 9.3% in FY26 and make up about two-thirds of business. Alkaline is nearly 10% of battery business (about 15% of category saliency per management) with volume growth over 20% CAGR; company alkaline share about 16%, up from under 10% a year ago.

segments.name: Flashlights
segments.commentary: Grew 3% in FY26 on a mature battery-operated base; rechargeables and new power bank and charger launches are the focus. BIS mandate fully implemented by end-January 2026 is seen favouring branded players.

segments.name: Lighting and electrical accessories
segments.commentary: Grew about 8.1% in FY26; management called the recent double-digit quarter-on-quarter growth sustainable. Flashlights and lighting with adjacencies make up about one-third of business.

segments.name: Mosquito racquets and mobile accessories
segments.commentary: Mosquito racquets, launched about 1.5 years ago, now hold a leadership position in urban markets; mobile accessories launched in FY26 via e-commerce.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin expected to be held around the FY26 level of 11.5%, with headwinds stronger than last year.
Zinc prices expected to keep rising into subsequent quarters; a further price increase may be needed in Q2 if cost volatility persists.
Jammu plant: commercial production in a few weeks, more than 100 million units in year one, phased ramp-up; operational breakeven from year one per CFO, payback 5-6 years.
Alkaline saliency expected to reach 20-25% of batteries in about 3 years, with zinc at 75%; company aims to exit with about 20% alkaline share.
Debt reduction to continue in FY27; no capex planned beyond routine capex; Plot B2 proceeds of about INR90 crore expected in FY27.
Tax: company expects to transition to Section 115BAA (22%) from FY27, subject to utilisation of carried-forward business losses.
A&P spend to stay at about 10% of sales.
capex_capacity: Jammu alkaline battery plant: investment about INR200 crore, peak capacity 360 million alkaline batteries per year, phased ramp-up; inaugurated 22 April 2026 by the J&K Lieutenant Governor.
Jammu also has lines for zinc batteries, flashlights and lighting products, enabling backward and forward integration.

Noida plant: exited, with Plot B1 leasehold transfer completed 30 March 2026 and Plot B2 pending; Noida plant closure is part of the manufacturing realignment begun in Q2 FY26 (November board meeting).
Jammu incentive (GST-linked) not yet approved; company is awaiting approval.
Depreciation impact of Jammu capitalisation not quantified; company will share details offline.
demand_pricing: Rural demand resilient through FY26; urban demand improved in the latter part of the year in value and everyday categories, but discretionary spending remains selective.
Zinc costs rose steeply and sustainedly in H2 FY26; calibrated price increases taken in carbon zinc and alkaline batteries.
INR ranged INR83 to INR91+ in FY26 and has moved to about INR94-95 recently; the company hedged FX and secured zinc positioning ahead of the market.
Flashlight market about 70% unbranded and China-dependent; BIS compliance expected to raise costs for unorganised importers in H2 CY26.
Management said H1 revenue is typically a few percentage points better than H2.
Urban revival may be at risk if West Asia-related disruption persists beyond Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How prepared is the business for INR94.5-95/USD and crude above $100, and what is the EBITDA margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FX hedging and zinc procurement positioning, plus pricing, delivered FY26. Management expects to hold margins around the 11.5% level in FY27, though headwinds are stronger than last year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the alkaline plant cannibalise carbon zinc, and will carbon zinc prices be raised to narrow the gap?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects alkaline at 20-25% and zinc at 75% of batteries in about 3 years, with some cannibalisation. The price gap in India is currently narrow, and further zinc price increases are possible.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 tax rate 22%, and why was there no tax on the Noida land sale?
qa_highlights.answer: Transition to 115BAA in FY27 is confirmed, subject to carried-forward business losses. The Noida gain was set off against about INR500 crore of business losses from the write-off of old ICD provisions; MAT credit not yet used.

qa_highlights.question: Is commercial production at Jammu starting in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Commercial production has not started yet; it is expected in a few weeks and within the current quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the target market share and export plan for Jammu?
qa_highlights.answer: Current alkaline share is about 16%, with a target of about 20% exit. Jammu output is for domestic sale for now, with white-label export possible later.

qa_highlights.question: Noida land sale proceeds versus the INR250 crore ballpark?
qa_highlights.answer: Plot B1 sold for about INR116 crore, with profit booked net of WDV and charges. Plot B2 is expected at about INR136 crore, with total about INR251 crore.

risks_watch: Zinc and crude-linked input cost inflation, plus INR weakness (INR94-95/USD), could pressure the 11.5% margin.
Jammu ramp-up and breakeven timing; depreciation impact not yet quantified.
Urban demand recovery could be affected if geopolitical disruption persists beyond Q1 FY27.
Tax rate transition to 22% depends on utilisation of carried-forward losses.
Governance: a non-executive promoter-nominee director's remuneration continues, and management could not commit to stopping it after he took an ED role elsewhere.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the strategic story (Jammu, alkaline premiumisation, BIS tailwind) but cautious on near-term costs; management repeatedly called the environment turbulent and avoided firm numbers on depreciation, tax and the director remuneration question.
key_quotes: So our sense is that from a breakeven point of view, I think between 5 to 6 years should be an ideal breakeven point for this plant going forward.
We are currently holding about 16% market share. And about a year back, it was less than 10%.
Debt reduction remains a clear priority, having reduced debt by more than INR100 crores in the current fiscal year.

rows.label: New product launch

tone.note: Management was confident on the Jammu alkaline plant, premiumisation and BIS tailwind but cautious on zinc, INR and margin headwinds, and avoided firm numbers on depreciation, tax and the director remuneration question; analysts pushed on margin trajectory, cannibalisation and the Jammu timeline.
